back_translation: O Israel, if you will return, then return to Me, declares the LORD. If you will remove your detestable things from My sight and not waver away again,
and if you swear, 'As surely as the LORD lives,' in truth, in justice, and in righteousness, then the nations will be blessed in Him, and in Him they will boast.
For the LORD says this to the men of Judah and Jerusalem: 'Plow up for yourselves the unplowed ground, and do not sow among thorns.'

O men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem, circumcise yourselves to the LORD and remove the foreskins of your hearts, lest My wrath break out like fire and burn with no one to quench it, because of your evil deeds.
Announce in Judah, proclaim in Jerusalem, and say, 'Blow the ram's horn throughout the land; cry aloud and say, Assemble yourselves, and let us flee into the fortified cities.'
Raise a signal flag toward Zion; flee for safety, do not stand still! For I am bringing disaster from the north, and great destruction.
A lion has come up out of his thicket, a destroyer of nations has set out; he has gone out from his place to make your land a desolation. Your cities will be destroyed, with no inhabitant.
Because of this, gird yourselves with sackcloth, wail and lament, for the fierce anger of the LORD has not turned away from us.
The LORD declares: 'In that day the king and the officials will lose their courage; the priests will be appalled, and the prophets will be dumbfounded.'
Then I said, 'O Lord GOD, truly You have let this people and Jerusalem be utterly deceived, with someone saying, You will have peace, while the sword has reached the throat.'
At that time it will be said to this people and to Jerusalem, 'A scorching wind from the bare heights in the desert blows toward the daughter of My people, not to winnow and not to cleanse.'
A wind stronger than that comes at My command. Now I Myself will pronounce judgments against them.
Behold, the enemy advances like clouds; his chariots are like a whirlwind, his horses swifter than eagles. Woe to us, for we are ruined!
O Jerusalem, wash your heart clean of evil, so that you may be saved. How long will you let wicked thoughts lodge within you?
For a voice proclaims from Dan, and announces disaster from the hill country of Ephraim.
Make it known to the nations; behold, proclaim concerning Jerusalem: 'A besieging army comes from a distant land, and they raise their voices against the cities of Judah.'
They surround her on every side like watchmen of a field, because she has rebelled against Me, declares the LORD.
Your ways and your deeds have brought these things upon you. This is your calamity; how bitter it is, for it reaches to your heart.
Oh, my heart, my heart! I writhe in pain! Oh, the walls of my heart! My heart pounds within me; I cannot keep silent, for I have heard the sound of the ram's horn, the alarm of war.
Disaster upon disaster is proclaimed, for the whole land is laid waste. My tents are destroyed in an instant, my tent-curtains in a moment.
How long must I see the signal flag and hear the sound of the ram's horn?
For My people are foolish; they do not know Me. They are senseless children, and they have no understanding. They are skilled at doing evil, but they do not know how to do good.
I looked at the earth, and behold, it was formless and void; and at the heavens, and they had no light.
I looked at the mountains, and behold, they were quaking, and all the hills were swaying.
I looked, and behold, there was no man, and all the birds of the sky had fled.
I looked, and behold, the fruitful land had become a wilderness, and all its cities were torn down before the LORD, before His fierce anger.
For the LORD says this: 'The whole land will be a desolation, but I will not make a full end of it.'
Because of this the earth will mourn, and the heavens above will grow dark, for I have spoken, I have purposed, and I will not relent or turn back from it.
At the sound of the horseman and the archer, every city flees. They go into the thickets and climb up among the rocks. Every city is abandoned, and no one lives in them.

And you, O devastated one, what will you do? Though you dress in scarlet, though you adorn yourself with gold ornaments, though you enlarge your eyes with paint, you beautify yourself in vain. Your lovers despise you; they seek your life.

For I have heard a cry like that of a woman in labor, anguish like a woman bearing her first child — the cry of the Daughter of Zion gasping for breath, stretching out her hands: 'Woe is me, for my soul faints before the murderers!'
